text:
Aisha: Quick postmortem follow-up from the streaming upload duplication incident. TL;DR: edge retried after midstream backend reset and downstream applied two writes.
Tom: Can someone summarize why the edge retried instead of surfacing a hard error? I thought we only retried idempotent methods.
Ravi: Edge treated the backend EOStream (connection reset) as transient and restarted the route. Our retry rules currently look at transport errors only, not semantic payload state.
Lena: Two orthogonal things: retry decision + dedupe capability. Even if we retry, the backend must be able to dedupe. We don't have a contract for that for streaming requests.
Chris: Proposal: introduce a lightweight checkpointing header for large uploads: X-RW-Stream-Checkpoint: <sha-offset>. Backend can persist checkpoints and reject duplicate segments.
Aisha: I don't love adding checkpointing for arbitrary backends. Alternate: require Idempotency-Key for any write-like stream and refuse retry if absent. Simpler.
Tom: If we refuse retries, we hurt tail latency for flaky infra. Ops will see more 5xxs. Can we make it opt-in per-route?
Ravi: Yes. Add route flag `stream_retry: allowed|forbidden|resume_capable`. Default forbidden for external origins.
Lena: For resume_capable routes we define a contract: 1) backend emits a trailer JSON: {"last_ack":"sha256:..","offset":<n>} 2) edge caches the last_ack for the Idempotency-Key and uses client Resume-After header on retry.
Chris: Edge needs to surface a small KV to backends (stream-shard lease) so backends can atomically claim a resume token. That suggests we only support resume for Redwood-hosted services.
Aisha: Agreed. We'll gate resume support to internal backends and documented via routing metadata. External upstreams must set Idempotency-Key or opt out of retry.
Tom: Operational concerns: memory and runtime. If we cache resume tokens/offsets per stream, what's the TTL and cardinality? High-volume uploads could blow memcache.
Ravi: TTL should be small (minutes). Also store only a compact resume token -> backend endpoint mapping, not full payload. We can rate-limit resume-enabled routes and reject too many concurrent streams.
Lena: Another axis is backpressure: hedging + resume is complex. If we hedge a streaming write, which copy wins? We must have a single-writer contract. Hedge only for read-like streams.
Chris: Good point. Hedge disabled for side-effecting streaming methods. We already have a header x-redwood-side-effect. Use that.
Aisha: Actionable checklist: - TOM: add route flag `stream_retry` and enforce no automatic retry for side-effecting streams unless route is resume_capable. - RAVI: prototype simple resume token flow and trailer format (suggested trailer: --rw-trailer\nContent-Type: application/json\n{"resume_token":"sha256:...","offset":123456}\n). - LENA: update routing metadata schema and console UI to show resume_capable. - CHRIS: add metrics: edge_streams{state="retries_blocked"} and edge_stream_resume_attempts_total.
Tom: For enforcement: edge will 422 if POST/PATCH/PUT with Transfer-Encoding: chunked and no Idempotency-Key when route.resume is forbidden. Sample config snippet: ````
route:
  stream_retry: forbidden
  require_idempotency_for_streams: true
````
Ravi: For the RFC I'll include a simple handshake: client sends Stream-Id + Idempotency-Key. Backend may return partial ACK trailers. On retry the client sends Resume-From header with the offset and same Idempotency-Key. Edge validates resume token matches cached token.
Lena: UX: SDKs should retry transparently only for resume_capable flows. Otherwise surface a clear error recommending adding Idempotency-Key or enabling resume on route.
Chris: Security: resume tokens must be opaque HMACs to avoid replay. Use HMAC(route-secret, stream-id||offset). We'll rotate keys.
Aisha: SLO impact: blocking retries increases 99p lat by returning error quickly, but avoids costly dedupe incidents. Ops: add alert if "sum(edge_duplicate_side_effects_total) > 0".
ops-bot: deploy 2024-10-03T09:12:00Z: edge-proxy@canary -> canary (sha: a1b2c3) :rocket:
Tom: Timeline: I'll land infra change (config + enforcement) in canary this week, Ravi aims for RFC + small proxy resume impl next sprint. Lena will coordinate console updates.
Ravi: One more: consider webhook producers. They often POST streaming payloads to many third parties. We'll document a webhook-safe mode: add `X-RW-WebHook-Idempotent: true` and a `webhook_mode` route flag that disables hedging and allows idempotency-only retry.
Aisha: Nice. If we can't get broad resume adoption, idempotency + route gating is good enough. We'll re-evaluate after two weeks of canary metrics.
Tom: Opening a PR with the enforcement rule + unit tests now. I'll also add an e2e job that simulates midstream reset + client resume behavior.
Lena: I'll draft a short runbook snippet: how to investigate duplicate-stream incidents (traces to check: edge.request_id, backend.stream_id, db-write-id).
Aisha: Thanks all. We'll meet after the canary run to decide whether to flip defaults.
